title: Trace Cache vs Conventional L1 Instruction Cache
decision: Implemented trace cache to replace traditional L1 instruction cache
rationale: Reduces branch misprediction penalties and improves instruction fetch bandwidth by storing pre-decoded dynamic instruction sequences
outcome: Higher IPC through more efficient instruction delivery
weakest_point: Cannot confirm the paper explicitly states the alternative was formally considered or rejected

title: Double-Pumped ALU Implementation
decision: Used double-pumped ALUs for simple integer and floating-point operations
rationale: Allows ALUs to operate at twice the core clock frequency, maintaining throughput in a deep pipeline without increasing power disproportionately
outcome: Preserved ALU throughput at high clock rates
weakest_point: Whether the paper uses the term 'double-pumped' or describes the mechanism differently

title: 20-Stage Pipeline Depth Selection
rationale: Enables very high clock frequencies by breaking down operations into smaller, more balanced pipeline stages
outcome: Achieved industry-leading clock speeds for the era
weakest_point: Exact stage count and whether it was presented as an explicit trade-off decision

title: Rapid Execution Engine Design
decision: Implemented rapid execution engine with fast, specialized ALUs for common operations
rationale: Reduces execution latency for frequently used operations, improving single-thread performance
outcome: Improved performance on common workloads despite deep pipeline
weakest_point: Specific name 'rapid execution engine' and its exact role as described in the paper

title: Memory Hierarchy Optimization for High Frequency
decision: Optimized L1 data cache size and associativity for high-frequency operation
rationale: Balances hit rate and access latency to sustain performance in a deep-pipeline, high-clock-frequency design
outcome: Efficient memory access supporting the aggressive clock targets
weakest_point: Specific cache parameters and whether they were framed as deliberate design choices
